topic_brief.title: No-till vs conventional tillage effects on crop yield
topic_brief.research_question: Does no-till management affect crop yield compared to conventional tillage, and how does this vary by crop type and climate?
topic_brief.population_description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing tillage systems
topic_brief.intervention_description: No-till or zero-till management (seeds planted directly into undisturbed soil)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional tillage (moldboard plow, disk, chisel, or other inversion/intensive tillage)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is NO-TILL (less disturbance), Control is CONVENTIONAL TILLAGE (more disturbance)
Reduced tillage is NOT no-till - if both exist, compare no-till vs conventional
Some papers have 3+ tillage levels - extract the no-till vs most intensive tillage comparison
Strip-till is intermediate - do not include as no-till unless paper explicitly calls it no-till
Long-term trials may show different effects in early vs late years - extract each year separately
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall -5.7%; Wheat -2.6%; Maize -7.6%; Rice -7.5%; Soybean +0.3%; Oilseed rape -9.0%

rows.title: Impact of conservation agriculture on soil organic carbon and crop productivity in cereal-based cropping systems
rows.treatment_description: Zero tillage with full residue retention (T3)
rows.control_description: Conventional tillage with residue removal (T1)
rows.notes: SEm(±) is pooled standard error of means from ANOVA (√(MSE/r), r=4 reps). CD(P=0.05)=0.37 is LSD. Paper does not separate rice and wheat yields — reports combined cereal system yield. Positive effect contradicts typical negative no-till effect; 5-year duration with residue retention in subtropical India may explain. T3 is zero tillage only (no crop diversification component).

rows.title: Impact of conservation agriculture on soil organic carbon and crop productivity in cereal-based cropping systems
rows.treatment_description: Full conservation agriculture: zero tillage + residue retention + crop rotation (T4)
rows.control_description: Conventional tillage with residue removal (T1)
rows.notes: SEm(±) is pooled standard error of means from ANOVA (√(MSE/r), r=4 reps). CD(P=0.05)=0.37 is LSD. T4 includes all three CA pillars: zero tillage, residue retention, AND crop diversification — more than just no-till. Paper does not separate rice vs wheat yields. Strong positive effect (+22.7%) noted in abstract.

rows.title: Response of Wheat Cultivar under Conservation Agriculture
rows.treatment_description: Zero tillage (ZT) - direct drilling with zero-till ferti-seed drill into rice residues
rows.control_description: Conventional tillage (CT) - disc plough + 2x disc harrow + rotavator + planking
rows.notes: Main effect of tillage averaged across 5 varieties and 5 nutrient-residue combinations. SE(m)=21.075 is standard error of tillage means from split-split plot ANOVA. CD(0.05)=82.284 (LSD). Difference ZT-CT=727.48 exceeds CD=82.284, confirming significance at p<0.05. Replication number not stated in paper. Unusually large positive effect (+46%) likely due to earlier sowing advantage of ZT in rice-wheat system and single-season trial.

rows.treatment_description: Zero tillage (direct seeding, no soil disturbance), pooled across residue treatments
rows.control_description: Conventional tillage (two harrowings + planking), pooled across residue treatments
rows.notes: Pooled analysis of 4 years (2015-16 to 2018-19). Split plot design with 4 replications. S.Em± = 46 and CD(P=0.05) = 142 are for tillage main effect means averaged over both residue levels. Zero tillage significantly lower than conventional tillage (CD = 142 kg/ha). Reduced tillage (1127 kg/ha) was at par with conventional tillage.

rows.treatment_description: Zero tillage without crop residue retention

rows.title: Energy Requirements and Performance of Different Soil Tillage Systems on the Yield of Maize Crop
rows.treatment_description: Zero tillage (direct drill, no soil disturbance)
rows.control_description: Conventional tillage (disc harrow + cultivator)
rows.notes: Three tillage systems compared: deep tillage (sub soiler + moldboard plow), conventional tillage (disc harrow + cultivator), zero tillage (drill). Yield values stated explicitly in text: DT=5727, CT=5108, ZT=4281 kg/ha. Three replications in RCBD. LSD at 0.05 used for mean separation but no numeric LSD value reported. No SE or SD values given anywhere in the paper. This observation is ZT vs CT (standard no-till vs conventional comparison).

rows.title: Energy Requirements and Performance of Different Soil Tillage Systems on the Yield of Maize Crop
rows.treatment_description: Zero tillage (direct drill, no soil disturbance)
rows.control_description: Deep tillage (sub soiler + moldboard plow, most intensive tillage)
rows.notes: This observation is ZT vs DT (no-till vs most intensive tillage in the study). Deep tillage uses sub soiler + moldboard plow which is the most intensive tillage in this 3-treatment study. Yield values stated explicitly in text. No numeric variance values reported despite LSD being mentioned as the statistical method.
